note: Static read+grep sweep of frontend/packages/{ui-kit,shared,sitemap,screen-map,dev-panel}. Most surfaces are clean: no `as any`/`as unknown` outside tests, only legitimate error-boundary console.error (ui-kit/AccessibilityProvider) and a CLI generator console.log (sitemap/json/generate.ts), all localStorage access try/catch-guarded, errors.ts retry-after parser NaN-guarded, and validation.ts date validators correctly guard Invalid Date via `Number.isNaN(d.getTime())`. Two net-new correctness findings both land in @ppt/shared (imported by ppt-web, mobile, reality-web) and both stem from the SAME root cause the codebase guards against elsewhere but omits here: unvalidated runtime data trusted against a TS type. Capped at 2 (both medium); no filler nits emitted.

evidence: frontend/packages/shared/src/auth.ts:60-81 decodeJwt() does `JSON.parse(jsonPayload) as JwtPayload` — a cast, not validation — so the decoded payload is trusted against the type without checking any claim is actually present or well-typed. JwtPayload declares `exp: number` (auth.ts:26 — required, non-optional), but a token whose payload omits `exp` (or carries a non-numeric exp) yields `payload.exp === undefined` at runtime while satisfying the compiler via the `as` cast.

frontend/packages/shared/src/auth.ts:90-98 isTokenExpired() then evaluates `payload.exp <= now + bufferSeconds` = `undefined <= number` = `false`, so an exp-less token is reported NOT expired (valid forever) — the exact inverse of the documented contract ('returns true if expired or invalid'). This is a client-side token-expiry BYPASS: auto-logout-on-expiry never fires and the app keeps using/refreshing a token it should reject. Same root defect leaks into getTokenExpiration() (auth.ts:106-113 -> `new Date(undefined*1000)` = Invalid Date object instead of the documented null) and getTokenRemainingTime() (auth.ts:121-129 -> `Math.max(0, undefined - now)` = NaN instead of the documented 0/-1). Fix: validate typeof payload.exp === 'number' && Number.isFinite(payload.exp) in decodeJwt (return null otherwise), mirroring the Number.isNaN(getTime()) guard the sibling validation.ts date validators already use.
Reachable via any tampered/legacy localStorage token or any backend that ever issues an exp-less JWT; @ppt/shared is imported by ppt-web and mobile.

frontend/packages/shared/src/formatting.ts:93-98 toDate() does an unguarded `new Date(input)`, which returns an Invalid Date for a malformed or nullish timestamp string. Every date formatter feeds that straight into Intl without a NaN guard: formatDate (103-111), formatDetailedDate (116-124), formatDateTime (129-139), formatTime (144-151), formatRelativeTime (163-197) call `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(...).format(toDate(date))`, and formatISODate (156-158) calls `toDate(date).toISOString().split('T')[0]`.

`Intl.DateTimeFormat.prototype.format(<Invalid Date>)` throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`, and `<Invalid Date>.toISOString()` throws the same RangeError. So passing a malformed or absent API timestamp (e.g. an optional/nullable `createdAt` that arrives as '' , null-coerced, or a wrong-typed value) to any of these throws synchronously during render and crashes the component subtree unless an error boundary catches it — no graceful fallback string.

This is the same Invalid-Date hazard that the sibling frontend/packages/shared/src/validation.ts:300-350 date validators explicitly guard with `Number.isNaN(d.getTime())`; the formatters omit that guard. Fix: in toDate (or each formatter) detect `Number.isNaN(d.getTime())` and return a safe placeholder (e.g. '' or '—') instead of throwing. @ppt/shared formatters are used across ppt-web, reality-web and mobile.
